subject: science
passage: As the climate warms, mountain glaciers around the world are losing ice. In the Himalayas, satellite images show that many glaciers have shrunk and pulled back over recent decades. Some writers conclude that every glacier in the high mountains of South and Central Asia is now retreating.
passage_b: In the Karakoram range of northern Pakistan, the record is surprisingly mixed. Since the 1990s, glaciologists have found that many glaciers there have stayed about the same size, and some have even grown slightly. Researchers are still testing explanations for this "Karakoram anomaly," such as heavier winter snowfall and cooler summers in the region, but none of them doubt that most of the world's glaciers are shrinking.
stem: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the conclusion in Text 1?

choices.A: By arguing that satellite images of Himalayan glaciers are unreliable
choices.B: By rejecting the idea that most of the world's glaciers are losing ice
choices.C: By accepting the general trend while pointing out a region where it does not hold
choices.D: By claiming that glaciers in the Karakoram are growing faster than others are shrinking

explanation.why: Text 1 ends with the conclusion that "every glacier" in the high mountains of South and Central Asia is retreating. Text 2 reports that many Karakoram glaciers "have stayed about the same size" and some have grown, though no researcher doubts "that most of the world's glaciers are shrinking." So Text 2 accepts the overall trend but rejects the word "every."
explanation.A: Incorrect. Text 2 never questions the Himalayan satellite images; it discusses a different range.
explanation.B: Incorrect. Text 2 says researchers do not "doubt that most of the world's glaciers are shrinking."
explanation.C: Correct. Text 2 agrees that most glaciers are shrinking but gives the Karakoram as an exception to Text 1's claim about "every glacier."
explanation.D: Incorrect. Text 2 says only that some Karakoram glaciers have grown "slightly"; it makes no comparison with the losses elsewhere.
